title: On-Prem Cluster Bootstrap Runbook (bare-metal + vSphere) - Draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook for bootstrapping on-prem Kubernetes clusters for Redwood Private deployments. It covers two main target platforms: (1) bare-metal with PXE/iPXE + MetalLB + local storage, and (2) vSphere (vCenter) based clusters. The goal is a repeatable, audit-friendly set of steps that the infra engineer or solutions lead can follow, plus notes for Terraform module integration and upgrade/rollback planning.

Audience:
- Platform engineers and SREs responsible for customer private deployments
- Solutions engineers preparing an on-prem installation for a customer
- Field ops teams performing upgrades/patching

Scope / Assumptions:
- Customer provides network, VLANs, IP ranges, and access to vCenter (if vSphere) or BMC/IPMI (if bare-metal).
- We expect an internal jump host with kubectl/terraform/helm installed.
- PKI: either customer-managed CA or our ephemeral CA via cert-manager (explicitly agreed).
- Bring-your-own-storage unless otherwise specified (we include instructions for local PVs + Rook/Ceph for durable workloads).

Quick Decisions to Make (pre-bootstrap):
- Control-plane topology: single-node control plane vs HA (3 control plane nodes)
- Etcd placement: stacked vs external
- Load balancer: MetalLB (bare-metal) or NSX/HAProxy (vSphere customers)
- Networking CNI: Calico (preferred), Cilium (optional if agreed)
- Container runtime: containerd (default)

Inventory checklist (required before starting):
- Node list (FQDN/asset id), CPU, RAM, disk mapping
- IP allocations: control-plane VIP, POD CIDR, Service CIDR, node mgmt IPs
- DNS entries to be created (api.cluster.example.com, *.apps.cluster.example.com)
- vCenter credentials + datacenter/cluster names (if vSphere)
- BMC credentials for automated provisioning (if bare-metal)

Bootstrap flow (high level):
1) Pre-flight checks: verify network connectivity, DNS, NTP, and access to registries.
2) Prepare terraform state and variables file (see Terraform notes below).
3) Provision VMs or bare-metal nodes (PXE or vSphere) with base OS image (Ubuntu 22.04 LTS).
4) Configure OS hardening and container runtime (disable swap, set sysctl, install containerd).
5) Install load balancer (MetalLB in layer2 mode or setup external LB).
6) Install control plane (kubeadm or k0s/k3s alternative). For HA clusters use kubeadm with stacked etcd or k0s for simplified HA.
7) Join worker nodes.
8) Install Redwood Private components (operator, control plane agents) via Helm charts—use imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent for air-gapped installs.
9) Post-install smoke tests (api server reachable, schedule pods, basic inference workload).

Detailed Steps and Commands (examples / snippets):
- Preflight (sample):
  - ssh jump@host 
  - curl -fsSL -o get-terraform.sh https://releases.hashicorp.com/terraform/1.5.6/terraform_1.5.6_linux_amd64.zip || note: pin version in tfvars
  - ntpdate -q 10.0.0.1 || echo "time drift check"

- kubeadm HA control-plane (short form):
  - kubeadm init phase upload-certs --upload-certs --config /tmp/kubeadm-cluster.yaml
  - kubeadm init --config /tmp/kubeadm-cluster.yaml
  - kubeadm join <control-plane-ip>:6443 --token <token> --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:<hash> --control-plane --certificate-key <key>

- Generate join token (if using ephemeral flow):
  - kubeadm token create --print-join-command

Air-gapped / registry mirror notes:
- Pre-pull images to local registry (registry.local:5000) and rewrite Helm image repository values.
- Export tarballs: crictl pull ... && ctr images export ...
- Ensure imagePullSecrets are created in target namespaces.

Storage notes (common patterns):
- Preferred quick option: local-path-provisioner for dev/test.
- Durable option: Rook Ceph (recommended when customer requires durable storage and multiple nodes).
- vSphere: use vSphere CSI with vCenter credentials and storage policy names.

Terraform modules notes (developer-facing):
- Module names in infra repo: infra-terraform/modules/vsphere-cluster and infra-terraform/modules/baremetal-provision.
- Expected variables: cluster_name, control_plane_count, worker_count, pod_cidr, service_cidr, vip_address, datastore, network_name, ssh_key_fingerprint.
- State backend: remote s3/Minio with locking via dynamodb or etcd (customer-managed). For air-gapped customers we recommend a secure S3 endpoint inside customer network.
- Outputs to consume in automation: kubeconfig_path, api_vip, loadbalancer_ips, node_ips.
- Note: make module idempotent for partial reprovision – use lifecycle ignore_changes for node labels we manage post-join.

Upgrade plan (cluster upgrades):
- Upgrade policy: Control-plane first, then kube-proxy/daemonsets, then workers in rolling fashion, then application pods.
- Target window: schedule maintenance, drain node, cordon, upgrade kubelet, kubeadm upgrade apply, uncordon.
- Specific steps (example v1.25 -> v1.26):
  1) Verify control-plane backup (etcd snapshot): ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.key
  2) Push snapshot to secure artifact store.
  3) kubeadm upgrade plan && kubeadm upgrade apply v1.26.3
  4) Restart control plane static pods where required.
  5) Upgrade kubelet and kubectl on nodes (apt/yum or package repo configured).
  6) Drain and upgrade workers in small batches (max surge policy per worker pool).

Rollback / safety:
- If control-plane fails to come back: restore etcd snapshot to a recovery cluster, drain traffic, and switch LB to standby cluster.
- Application rollback: maintain previous image tag in private registry to re-deploy if CR replacement fails.
- Terraform rollback: use terraform state rm/apply carefully – prefer manual operator actions over force-destroy in customer environments.

Validation and smoke tests (post bootstrap / post-upgrade):
- kubectl get cs (componentstatuses) and kubectl get nodes --show-labels
- Run a small inference pod that hits model container and verifies latency < configured SLA for baseline.
- Run e2e smoke: helm test redwood-operator or ./scripts/smoke-test.sh --kubeconfig /path/to/kubeconfig

Observability and logging setup:
- Install Prometheus + Grafana (short retention for small installs).
- Ensure node exporter and kube-state-metrics are deployed.
- Fluentd/Fluent Bit to forward to customer ELK or our optional aggregator.

Known issues / caveats (notes):
- vSphere CPI CSI versions must match vCenter API compatibility matrix — verify before upgrade.
- MetalLB ARP conflicts on networks with strict switch anti-spoofing policies.
- k0s currently has different kubeadm token handling; document if chosen.

Open TODOs / questions to resolve before finalizing runbook:
- Decide default recommendation for small-footprint customers: k0s vs kubeadm? (PD-3234 ticket)
- Add step-by-step PXE templates for Ubuntu 24.04 if requested by field ops.
- Formalize certificate rotation runbook and integrate with cert-manager (automated) or Ansible (manual).

Appendix: Useful links and snippets
- Terraform PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-terraform/pull/482
- Example kubeadm config template: /repos/infra-templates/kubeadm-templates/ha-controlplane.yaml (internal repo)
- Sample smoke-test repo: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tests/smoke-cluster

Quick-run checklist (minimal):
- [ ] Confirm inventory, VLANs, DNS, NTP
- [ ] Prepare terraform tfvars + state backend
- [ ] Provision nodes (PXE/vSphere)
- [ ] OS + containerd hardening
- [ ] Install LB (MetalLB/external)
- [ ] kubeadm init / control-plane joins
- [ ] Join workers
- [ ] Helm install redwood-operator + agents
- [ ] Run smoke tests and collect baseline metrics

Notes to self (informal):
- When doing a live customer bootstrap, keep RFC/maintenance page open and record timestamps for each major step.
- Capture cloud-init snippets used so we can convert to terraform module later rather than manual SSH steps.

Contact / escalation:
- Primary: Priya Kapoor (owner)
- Backup: Ethan Morales (eng-sre)
- Escalation: Zoe Chen (platform eng lead)

End of draft runbook.
